statements: CREATE TABLE users AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS user_id, (20 + i)::INTEGER AS age, ['US', 'DE', 'IN'][1 + i % 3] AS country FROM range(8) t(i)
CREATE TABLE orders AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS order_id, (i % 8)::BIGINT AS user_id, (10 + i * 1.5)::DOUBLE AS price, TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' + to_days((i * 7)::INTEGER) AS ts FROM range(80) t(i)
CREATE TABLE addresses (aid BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, city VARCHAR, tag BIGINT)
CREATE TABLE customers (cid BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, aid BIGINT REFERENCES addresses (aid), seg VARCHAR, tag BIGINT)
CREATE TABLE orders (oid BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, cid BIGINT REFERENCES customers (cid), aid BIGINT REFERENCES addresses (aid), pid BIGINT, sid BIGINT, ts TIMESTAMP, tag BIGINT)
INSERT INTO addresses SELECT i AS aid, ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'][1 + i] AS city, i AS tag FROM range(5) t(i)
INSERT INTO customers SELECT i AS cid, i % 5 AS aid, ['x', 'y'][1 + i % 2] AS seg, i AS tag FROM range(10) t(i)
INSERT INTO orders SELECT i AS oid, i % 10 AS cid, (i + 2) % 5 AS aid, i % 6 AS pid, i % 3 AS sid, TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' + to_days(i::INTEGER) AS ts, i AS tag FROM range(40) t(i)
pql: PREDICT COUNT(orders.*, 0, 30, days) FOR EACH addresses.aid
